eyebrow: A one-line recap, then real depth
code:
System Administration Lesson 9:
  "Elevate Roles turns on security_admin
   so you can edit an ACL record."

This lesson: WHY that bypass is scoped
so narrowly, and WHY it's dangerous enough
to deserve its own governance practice.
caption: A troubleshooting detail, revisited as a security control.

code:
Normal ACL evaluation:              With security_admin elevated:
Every table's ACL script runs       Editing sys_security_acl
  for every user, every op            records specifically bypasses
                                       ACL script evaluation

Scope of bypass: narrow (ACL edits only)
Scope of consequence: platform-wide (ACLs govern everything else)
caption: A narrow bypass with platform-wide consequences if misused.

eyebrow: Why the bypass is so dangerous
code:
A user who can freely rewrite ACL records can:
  - grant themselves access to a restricted table
  - remove a role requirement protecting sensitive data
  - widen a write ACL that was deliberately scoped narrow

One careless or malicious edit can open access
far beyond whatever the admin intended to fix.
caption: Rewriting the rules is never just a one-record change.

code:
If security_admin were permanent:
  every admin session, even routine ones,
  carries a live ability to rewrite
  platform-wide access rules

Elevate Roles instead:
  activates it for THIS session only,
  on purpose, only when actually needed
caption: Scoping the window shrinks the blast radius for everyday work.
